evidence: Start: after the clef and key signature, the first group is five repeated notes (16th, 8th, 8th, 8th, 16th) followed by a barline. Start: the line opens with four groups of repeated A3 32nds and no rests. That fits the second half of bar 85, whose rests and first 32nds were on the previous line. The line ends with bar 90, not 91. Its last bar has rest, two eighths, rest, rest, two eighths, rest. That is the B3-B3 / E4-E4 pattern of bar 90, and the final barline closes the line there. Start: the line's first bar (marked p.) has three quarters, F3, E3 and D3, then a quarter rest. This matches bar 60, and bar 61 follows with C3 8th, C4 dotted 16th, C3 32nd, B2, B3, A2 under f. The program's range is wrong; the line holds bars 60 to 67. At the start, the line opens (marked p.) with three quarter notes and a quarter rest: F3 E3 D3, rest. That is bar 60. The line opens with the end of bar 68, not bar 69. Right after the clef and key signature come four 16ths (A3 F3 G3 A3), a trilled B3–C4–B3 figure, then an A3 8th, an 8th rest and a quarter rest. The line probably holds bars 34–40, so the claimed start of bar 35 is likely wrong; the end is right. Start is correct. Before the first barline are two beamed groups of eight 32nds with a sharp near the end of the first. The match is right: the line holds bars 40 to 45. At the start, the first three dense beamed 32nd-note groups and the grace-note figure (B5 grace, then A5, G5, F5) come before the first barline. The line starts before bar 41. Before the first barline (about x≈450) there are 32nd-note groups of repeated notes, ending with a grace note plus a 16th and two 32nds. Not right: the line starts before bar 45. Before the first barline there is a short fragment, which is the end of bar 43. Start: the line opens (after the clef and key signature) with the end of bar 45: a beamed figure, then an eighth, a 16th rest and three repeated 16th notes. This matches 'C5 8th, rest 16th, C5 16th ×3'. After the first barline come bar 46's four grace-note groups and its descending 32nd run. The line opens with two quarter notes under 'dolce', then a barline, then a sharpened quarter followed by 8th, 8th, dotted 8th + 16th, 8th, 8th. That second figure is bar 50 (G#4 quarter, G4 G4, G4. A4, G4 G4). So the two opening quarters are the B4–A4 quarters that close bar 49, and the line starts with the tail of bar 49. The start is right. Before the first barline the line has two quarters, B4 and A4, which end bar 49. Next comes G#4 quarter, G4 8th, G4 8th, G4 dotted 8th, A4 16th, G4 8th, G4 8th, which is bar 50. After it come three bars of paired arpeggio figures with trills on the repeated top notes: F5-D5-A4-D5 F5 F5 F5 and G5-E5-C5-E5 G5 G5 G5, then F5-D5-A4-D5 and E5-C5-A4-C5, then F5-D5-A4-D5 and G5-E5-C5-E5. Yes, bars 12 to 17 is right. Start: the line opens with a flat and an eighth note, then a short beamed figure. This fits the end of bar 12 (the flatted D-flat 8ths at the end of that bar). The line closes with bar 17: C5 dotted 8th, C4 16th, natural B3 quarter, A3 half. A repeat double bar then ends the line, before bar 18's 16th-note runs would begin.

The line does not hold bars 11–17. At the start, the first full bar after the opening fragment carries a natural and runs as an unbroken chain of sixteenths with a trill. That matches bar 18 (A4 B♮4 C#5 D5 C5 D5 E5 F5 E5 G#5 A5 G5, A5). It does not match bar 11's 32nd-note arpeggios broken by rests. So the opening fragment is around bar 17, not bar 11. At the end, the line continues through several more bars, including trills and grace-note figures like those of bars 19–20 and beyond, and closes with a repeat double bar. It therefore runs well past bar 17.

Start: before the first barline the line has only a dotted quarter and an eighth, high on the staff with 'cresc.'. That matches the end of bar 38 (G5 dotted quarter, B5 eighth). The start is right but the end is not. The line opens with an incomplete bar: a dotted quarter and an eighth under 'cresc.', then a barline. Start: after the clef, the line opens with a low two-note chord half (A3+G4), then single A4s with a dotted-8th + 16th figure. That is bar 86, not bar 85's run of eighths. The line does not begin in bar 85. After the clef it opens with a half-note double stop low on the staff, with ledger lines below. Start: the line opens with a lone eighth note followed by eighth rests, then a run of 32nds marked with a sharp (D#4 D4 D4 D4). This is the end of bar 16 (F4 8th, rests, D#4 32nds), so bar 16 is the first bar. Middle: after the first barline, the eight 4-note 32nd groups match bar 17: two groups of E4, a group of G4, a sharped A group, then A♮ written out where the edition has tremolo quarters. End: after the second barline come four low groups before the custos, which matches bar 18 (G G D# D tremolos), the last bar. Uncertainties: the copy shows no visible sharp in that final bar, and it has four groups where the edition's four tremolo quarters would suggest more, so the bar-18 match is the least certain part. Still, the line contains bars 16–18.

The start is right: the line opens with an eighth note and rests, then a sharpened 32nd group (D#4 D4 D4 D4). That is the second half of bar 16 (F4 8th, two 8th rests, D#4 32nds). The end is wrong. After the first barline come eight 32nd groups: E, E, G, A#–A–A–A, then a natural and three more A groups (the tremolo quarters written out). That is all of bar 17. After the next barline there are only four groups, i.e. half a bar, with 'cresc.' beneath. These are the first half of bar 18 (the G4, G4 tremolo quarters), and the line stops there. So the line covers bars 16–18; it does not reach bar 19.

The claim is wrong: the line holds bar 17 complete, and its music does not begin in bar 18. The section between the two barlines has eight beamed 32nd-note groups, with a sharp before the 4th group and a natural before the 5th. That is bar 17: E4 32nds, then G4, then A#4 A A A, then the A♮ tremolo quarters written out. The four 32nd groups before the first barline are the end of bar 16. After the second barline only two dotted 32nd groups begin bar 18 before the custos. So bar 18 is the line's last bar, and bar 20 is not on the line.

The start at bar 17 fits: the line opens with four low 32nd-note groups, matching bar 17's repeated E4s, then G/A, then the tremolo As. The end does not fit. After the 32nd-note groups for bars 18–19 (G, G, D#, D, then E, G…A#, A, A), a further barline is followed by two lighter groups of 16ths with staccato dots. These are the G-G-A-F-G-A-G-F figures of bar 20, followed by a custos. So the line runs into bar 20 rather than ending at bar 19.

The line has exactly two full bars, each made of eight groups of four 32nd notes on one repeated pitch. That is the written-out form of four tremolo quarter notes on G4, which matches bars 32 and 33. At the start, the first bar opens directly with the repeated 32nd groups and has no rests. Bar 31 would begin with a quarter rest, an 8th rest and four 32nd G4s before its tremolo quarters, so the line starts at bar 32. At the end, the second bar keeps the same single pitch through all eight groups and closes at the barline. Bar 34 would bring D#5 and D5 tremolos and then E5 8ths, so the line ends at bar 33. The cresc. under bar 32 and the f under the barline, followed by ff, fit this build-up.

The line opens with no rests, just eight groups of four repeated 32nds on G4 (eight eighth-beats, one full 4/4 bar) up to the first barline. Then come eight more identical groups and a final barline. This matches bars 32 and 33, which are each four tremolo quarters on G4. Bar 31 should start with a quarter rest and an eighth rest, followed by only four 32nds and two tremolo quarters (five groups); that does not appear here, so bar 31 belongs to the previous line. At the other end, the line stops at the barline after bar 33, before bar 34's D#5. So the line holds bars 32–33, not 31–33.

Start: the line opens with sharp-marked tremolo groups (D#5, D5 tremolo quarters) followed by two 8th–16th-rest–16th figures before the first barline, which is bar 34. End: after the second barline the line continues with 8th, rest, 8th rest, then 16th-note figures (G4 16th, G4 8th, G4 16th, G4 16ths). That is bar 36, not bar 35. So the line spans bars 34–36, and the claim of 34–35 misses bar 36 at the end.

The program's claim is wrong; the line spans bars 34 to 36. Start: right after the clef there is a sharp before the first group of beamed repeated 32nds. These written-out tremolos fill two quarters, matching bar 34's D#5 and D5 tremolo quarters. The figures that follow (E5 8th, 16th rest, 16th) and then the first barline also belong to bar 34. Middle: bar 35 comes after the first barline (G4 8th, rest, sharped D#5 16th, E5, then G4 8th/rest pairs). End: after the second barline, the line has G4 8th and rest, then the G4 16th-8th-16th figure and 16ths. That is bar 36, cut off before the bar finishes.

Start: the line opens with a sharp and four groups of 32nd-note tremolo, then a barline. That half-bar is the E#4 half note at the end of bar 50; the bar's D4/B3 32nds sit on the previous line. Middle: the full bar of eight groups is bar 51. Its first two groups are F4, then a natural marks the E♮4 groups, then a sharp marks the D#4 half. End: the last segment holds E4 (two groups), a natural for D♮4 (two groups), and then the line stops. Bar 52's C4 half continues on the next line. So the line runs from bar 50 to bar 52.

The line opens with a sharp and four groups of repeated 32nds, which is a written-out half note. That is the E#4 half closing bar 50, and a barline follows it, so bar 50 belongs to this line. Next come two groups (F4 quarter), then a natural and two groups (E♮4 quarter), then a sharp and four groups (D#4 half), which is bar 51 up to its barline. After that, two groups (E4 quarter) and a natural with two groups (D♮4 quarter) are bar 52's first half. Its C4 half, and bar 53's D4–E4, fall on the next line. So the line holds bars 50 to 52, not 51 to 53.

The line opens with four groups of 32nds (16 notes = a half note) before the first barline. These are the lowest notes on the line, about one ledger line below the staff. They fit the C4 half of bar 52, written out as repeated notes. The full middle bar has eight groups: the first four sit lower and the last four slightly higher, which fits bar 53 (D4 half, then E4 half). The line ends with four groups (a half note) at D4 height followed by a custos, matching the D4 half that opens bar 54, which the next line finishes. Bar 51 (F, E, D#, falling) would not fit the rising middle bar. This reading of the handwritten pitches is tentative, and bar 55 (also D, then E) would fit the middle bar too, so bars 53–55 cannot be fully ruled out. On balance the line most likely runs from the end of bar 52 to partway through bar 54.

The line has only three bar-units: four 32nd-note groups, a barline, eight groups, a barline, then four groups. The first unit sits low, below and on the bottom of the staff. Its written-out 32nds first stay on one low pitch and then drop further (D4 ×8, then B3 ×8), followed by more repeated 32nds for the E#4 half. That is bar 50, not bar 51. The second unit, on the bottom lines in eight groups, matches bar 51's F4–E4–D#4 tremolos written out. The final unit, four groups before the custos, matches bar 52 (E4, D4, C4). So the line runs from bar 50 to about bar 52, not 51 to 54. There is no room for bars 53–54.

The line does not hold bars 54–56; it holds bars 56–58. The middle segment, between the two barlines, has eight groups of four 32nds. That matches bar 57, which is 32 thirty-seconds, C C C C D D D D C C D D C C B B twice. Bar 54 is two tremolo halves (D4, C4), so it cannot be this. At the start, the four 32nd groups before the first barline match the second half of bar 56 (C C C C D D D D C C D D C C B B), most likely continuing bar 56's D4 tremolo half from the previous line. At the end, the line closes with four 32nd groups and no closing barline. That is the first half of bar 58 (C C D D C C B B ×2); its C4 eighth and rests continue on the next line.

The line opens with clef and key signature followed by 16 thirty-seconds before the first barline. They follow the pattern C4 C4 C4 C4, D4 D4 D4 D4, C4 C4 D4 D4, C4 C4 B3 B3, which is the second half of bar 56 (its D4 half-note tremolo falls on the previous line). There are no tremolo half notes on D4/E4 here, so bar 55 is absent. Between the barlines are 32 thirty-seconds repeating that figure, which is bar 57. After the second barline come 16 thirty-seconds (C C D D C C B B, twice), the first half of bar 58. Its closing C4 eighth and rests do not appear, so the line ends partway through bar 58. The line therefore covers bars 56–58, not 55–56.

Start: after the clef and key signature, the line opens with a one-bar whole rest marked '1'. That is bar 84 (rest whole), because bar 83 has 8th notes. Next comes the quarter rest and 8th rest, then pp 32nds, which is bar 85. The line does not begin with bar 83. After the clef and key signature it opens with a single whole-bar rest marked '1', which matches bar 84 (rest whole). Bar 83's notes (C4 8th, rests, C4 8th, rests) do not appear at all. Next comes a quarter rest, an 8th rest and pp 32nd-note groups, which is bar 85. At the right end the line breaks off in a bar of repeated-note tremolo groups after the f, consistent with bar 87. So the start is wrong: the line holds bars 84–87, not 83–87.

The line opens with a short bar of only two tremolo groups before the first barline. That matches the second half of bar 30, whose opening (the four G4 16ths and the first tremolo notes) would sit at the end of the previous line. Two full bars of four tremolo groups follow, each alternating B4 with G4/A4. These match bars 31 and 32. The line closes with the last G–A alternation of bar 32 and a barline, so bar 33's identical figure and bar 34's B4 quarter and rests start the next line. This reading assumes each manuscript group stands for two of the edition's tremolo notes; bars 31–33 are identical, so the short opening bar is what pins the start to bar 30.

The line opens with an incomplete bar of only two sixteenth-note tremolo groups (two quarter beats) before the first barline. It then has two full bars of four groups each, built from a repeated upper note over an alternating lower pair (B over G–A). Bar 29 is two half notes (A#4, A♮4), and no half notes appear anywhere on the line, so the line cannot begin in bar 29. The opening fragment is the end of a tremolo bar (30 or later), and the line ends after two more full tremolo bars. The 29–32 claim is therefore wrong at least at the start.

Start: the line opens with the bar of sixteenth-note groups on B4/G4/A4, which is bar 33 written as abbreviated tremolo. The following bars match bar 34 (rests), bar 35 (quarter rest, then E4 E4 E4, marked pp) and bar 36 (the D#4 whole note, shown as a sharp and open note).
